review.claim: The Sleep dialog (src/ui/shell/TimeControls.tsx SleepDialog, run('life.sleep', { hours }) at :175; it never sends startAt) sends life.sleep. The command refuses: hours that aren't a number ('Say how long to sleep.', life.ts:368); a start that isn't finite (:371), is in the past, or is more than a day ahead (:373); and a start inside a kept commitment, through occupiedAt (:374, 'You’re at X until Y.'). It clamps hours to [SHORTEST_SLEEP, 16], stamps lastSleptAt as the wake when the night is booked, advances to the start, reads sleepQuality (nightParts: stress, the sleepQuality knob, a late hour), sets awakeSince to the wake, and advances to the wake while the world runs. Then applySleep moves energy, sleepDebt, stress, condition, morale and nourishment, and wokeWithDebt is set (:409). If requiresPlayer items fall inside the night it posts 'You Slept Through N Commitment(s)' (:414-423). Downstream: a commitment slept through is missed (the PLAN_KIND asleep branch; school classes and sessions through present(); appointments through presentForCare; rehearsals and coursework through awakeSince); sleepAlone gives no second night; readiness feeds focusOf; the waking drain reads wokeWithDebt.

gapsOpen: partial: The plan's part of a bill is real and played. A played life with need reaches a program renewal by the clock alone (tests/need-paths.test.ts): she is withdrawn, enrolled in HUSKY D on Papers, and her renewal on 1 November 2027 passes the income test on interest alone, then fails Connecticut's 2027 work test, so HUSKY D ends and she's told. A renewal that keeps a program is reached too: an Inherited family's student enrolls in Covered Connecticut on a personal leave, on January's interest, and it renews on 1 September 2027 on August's interest, by play alone (tests/scope-cover.test.ts); need-paths plays HUSKY D moved to Covered Connecticut at renewal. Until the recheck of 2026-10-15 this said no renewal that keeps a program was reached and Covered Connecticut's couldn't be: that reckoning assumed a family with need and work-study income, and overlooked the interest an Inherited life earns. What stays open is HUSKY D kept at renewal through work: SLATE pays wages only for work-study and the Summer Cabaret, both a student's, so a life off Yale Health has none, and the tests give it as TEST SETUP wages. From the recheck, HUSKY D's work test reads the School over last month, as 42 CFR 435.552(c) has it, at an application and at a renewal; until then it read the School at the instant asked, and a student at the School all of January 2027, withdrawn on 1 February, was refused on 2 February. HUSKY D kept by her being at the School is played (tests/scope-cover.test.ts, back from a leave). No income was invented and no eligibility loosened.

defects.summary: A term deposit’s interest at maturity is not recorded as income. endTerm’s creditInterest (renewed or moved to savings) and the paid-out branch post the interest but never call recordInterest. So it is missing from the year’s earnings, which the return taxes, and from the month’s income, which programFor and mayEnroll read. An Inherited student with $2,849,566 in Chase’s CD is credited $57,928.16 on 24 March 2027, but March’s income reads $276. Enroll on 1 April gives HUSKY D (measured: kind 'medicaid', from 1 June 2027) where the marketplace is due. By contrast, a savings account’s monthly interest (banking.ts payInterest) and a CD’s interest taken by hand (bank.take_term_interest) are both recorded.

Still open, the latest skeptic's problem 1: HUSKY D kept at a renewal through 80 hours' work is reached only on a FIXTURE (tests/remaining-health-billing.test.ts). The program is set by hand from 1 March 2026 and the wages are posted by hand. I confirmed from the code that no played life reaches it. workedBetween (earnings.ts:207-219) counts only 'salary' postings. Only two exist, both in school.ts: work-study wages (:3369) and the Summer Cabaret stipend (:3954, counted as 40 hours). monthEngagement (health.ts:435-454) returns 'school' before it reads work. enrolledIn (:510-516) counts any month partly at the School, so the month of a withdrawal, a dismissal, the degree or a leave's start is 'school'. Work stops with the School: planWeek returns once it has ended (school.ts:1729), shiftRefusal refuses it and a leave (:1549-1557), startLeave calls off school.* items except the payday (leave.ts:162, :353), and the Summer Cabaret takes only a student in good standing, not on leave, with a year to come (school.ts:1534-1546). So a month wholly off the School can get only the last payday: work-study owed since the Friday before, at most about 29 hours under the 19-hour term cap, or one kept stipend at 40 counted hours. Elective shifts are only in a term (:4036), so the two don't come together. That is never 80.

Found here: even where the work arm is reached, it never decides an outcome, only the sentence. monthEngagement adds wages the record doesn't hold to the month's income (health.ts:445-447). Every TEST SETUP posting of the work arm is $600 for 80 hours (remaining-health-billing, need-paths, scope-cover, remaining-health-eligibility, evidence-g05-life), which meets the $580 income arm by itself. With the work arm cut, each is still kept or moved, and only the notice changes from 'by 80 hours’ work' to 'by its income, $580.00 or more'. That is how the recorded mutation B2b-work-kept (workHours + 1, remaining/health-billing-result.json) was killed: by the sentence. In play the two arms can't come apart either. SLATE pays $23 an hour for work-study and $375 a week for the stipend, so any 80 hours paid is well over $580. By the falsifiability test, the arm's hours change only the sentence. checks.json's health.month check said the same of the g05 test.

Decision: an arm play can't reach, held on a fixture, keeps the row partial under the standard. The latest skeptic named this arm. Verified needs every named problem closed by a test that reaches it as a player does, and nothing can. The standard's only other ways out are a defect shown fixed, or the owner removing or deferring the system. Neither applies. The house ruled the same on school.request_repeat and school.request_extra_term (final-checks zz-recheck and zzz-r3-school: fixture-only, unreachable, left partial as the owner's call under THE ONE RULE). It differs from documents.us_status (zzz-r3-lifepapers), which was verified because no review or check had named its unreachable branch. Here one did. Brief 11 §3 says relabeling isn't gameplay progress, and §10 says untested behavior isn't marked verified. So the row's text should say the arm is unreachable in play and, where reached, doesn't change the outcome, but saying so doesn't close it. The owner decides whether to cut the arm or keep it as a guard, with the row recording that decision.

review.claim: On the first of each month (health.month, armed by armHealth), healthMonth runs. It draws a new chronic condition at its yearly onset (onsetMonth). It ends a marketplace plan out of status. It renews a program on the income and work test or ends it with a notice. It charges Medi-Cal's premium, the marketplace premium (an unpaid one ends the plan, 'nonpayment') and a monthly dental premium. It runs keepUp (the month's care for treated conditions, lapsing those unpaid), records California's uncovered months, says 'Your Health Cover Ended' with or without a special enrollment, sets h.covered, and reports a year-old medical debt.

defects.summary: Connecticut's minimum compensation is held to 75% of the wage after tax, where CGS 31-307(a) holds it to 75% of the average weekly wage. The statute: no less than 20% of the maximum, 'provided the minimum payment shall not exceed seventy-five per cent of the employee's average weekly wage, as determined under section 31-310', which is gross wages. With the maximum at $1,776, any week under $473.60 should pay 75% of its gross. The Summer Cabaret's $375 stipend instead pays a resident 75% of $375 less a year of federal tax and FICA ($252.67), and an F-1 student $274.19, where both are owed $281.25.

problems: Nothing that breaks the claim. findings.what: An overturned appeal pays cash back for a bill the player never paid; the medical debt stays
findings.evidence: health.bill sets bill.paid=true before payFromCurrent; on failure it posts the full amount to the medical-debt account. Appeals are decided 60 days on, always after the 30-day due date, so bill.paid is always true by then. The refund posts `over` into the current account without reducing the debt account.
findings.suggestedFix: Track whether the bill was paid or went to debt (e.g. bill.unpaid). When it's in debt, credit the debt account by `over` (capped at its balance) instead of the current account

findings.what: Bills that went unpaid show 'Settled' on Papers
findings.evidence: paid=true is set for an unpaid bill too, and the UI prints b.paid ? 'Settled'
findings.suggestedFix: Set paid only on success; mark failures 'debt' and show that

findings.what: Therapy sessions count while asleep or in hospital
findings.evidence: The session handler checks location only. life.sleep warns 'You Slept Through 1 Commitment', yet the session is paid, counted, and can lift depression. Doctor appointments use present() and are missed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use health.ts:present(person, item.at, t.cityId); when absent, mark it missed and reschedule as for away

findings.what: Depression therapy is charged twice during a CBT course
findings.evidence: keepUp charges CHRONIC.therapyPerMonth (2) sessions a month for treated depression, whether or not person.therapy is running. The course charges each weekly session as well.
findings.suggestedFix: Skip keepUp's therapy cost while person.therapy is active, or let the course stand in for it

findings.what: health.treat toggle clears a lapse for free
findings.evidence: on:false then on:true sets lapsed=false with no payment, so keptUp is true again until the next health.month. That avoids the depression morale toll, diabetes condition toll and doubled asthma emergencies. Untreated through the 1st and re-treated after also skips the month's care.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep lapsed when re-treating, or charge the month's care on re-treat

findings.what: Workers' compensation can never happen in play
findings.evidence: No caller passes `work`, so injury.atWork is never set, injury.comp is never scheduled and WORKERS_COMP is reached only by tests calling compWeek directly
findings.suggestedFix: Wire the school stage call (or work-study) to pass work, or delete the dead path and its notice text

findings.what: Look After and Sleep are allowed from a hospital bed
findings.evidence: lookAfterRefusal and life.sleep never check inHospital. practice.ts:40 and engagement.ts:50 refuse with 'Not from a hospital bed.' A player admitted for a stay can work out (and roll a gym injury), shower or order in.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an inHospital(person, now) refusal to lookAfterRefusal (and probably exercise while fluUntil)

findings.what: Injury look says an injury takes condition; code never touches condition
